segments.he: מַתְנִי׳ דֶּרֶךְ תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים, עַד שֶׁלֹּא הָיְתָה בִּתּוֹ יוֹצְאָה מֵאֶצְלוֹ, אוֹמֵר לָהּ: כׇּל נְדָרִים שֶׁנָּדַרְתְּ בְּתוֹךְ בֵּיתִי — הֲרֵי הֵן מוּפָרִין. וְכֵן הַבַּעַל, עַד שֶׁלֹּא תִּכָּנֵס לִרְשׁוּתוֹ, אוֹמֵר לָהּ: כׇּל נְדָרִים שֶׁנָּדַרְתְּ עַד שֶׁלֹּא תִּכָּנְסִי לִרְשׁוּתִי — הֲרֵי הֵן מוּפָרִין. שֶׁמִּשֶּׁתִּכָּנֵס לִרְשׁוּתוֹ — אֵינוֹ יָכוֹל לְהָפֵר.
segments.en: «MISHNA:» «The practice of Torah scholars» is to ensure that a woman about to be married should not be encumbered by any vows. A father, «before his daughter would leave him» through marriage, «would say to her: All vows that you vowed in my house are hereby nullified. And similarly, the husband, before she would enter his jurisdiction,» i.e., while they were still betrothed, «would say to her: All vows that you vowed before you entered my jurisdiction are hereby nullified.» This was necessary «because once she enters his jurisdiction he cannot nullify» the vows she made before that.

moves.summary: father nullifies before she leaves his house
moves.about: scholars pre-emptively nullify a daughter's or bride's vows before marriage

moves.summary: betrothed nullifies before she enters his jurisdiction, since afterwards he cannot
